neighbours.label: in economics / policy writing, the modifier right before an expected 'model' or 'analysis' ('general equilibrium [model]', 'cost-benefit [analysis]', 'econometric [model]'); the pole's output promotes ' model' and ' analysis'. 'model' in other senses stays quiet.
fire: The ministry's forecast is based on a general equilibrium model of the national economy.
Before approving the dam, the bank required a cost-benefit analysis of the project.
The authors estimate the wage gap with an econometric model of the labour market.
The pension reform was studied with an overlapping-generations model of household saving.
Trade economists often use a computable general equilibrium model to assess tariffs.
The carbon tax was evaluated using a dynamic general equilibrium model with two sectors.
The treasury published a cost-benefit analysis of the proposed rail link.
Researchers built an agent-based model of the housing market to test the policy.
quiet: The ministry's forecast was announced at a crowded press conference.
Before approving the dam, the bank visited the valley twice.
The architect showed a scale model of the new rail station.
The agency hired a fashion model for its winter campaign.
Trade economists often disagree about the effect of tariffs.
The carbon tax raised fuel prices in both sectors.
The treasury published a short statement about the proposed rail link.
Researchers interviewed tenants and landlords about the housing market.

notes: Card: top examples sit just before 'model' / 'analysis' in economics text (DICE) model, benefit-cost analysis, simulation model, agent-based model), and the - pole's output promotes ' analysis', ' model', ' modeling'. Probes: 'general equilibrium' 0.41-0.58, 'overlapping-generations' 0.48, 'econometric' 0.37, 'cost-benefit' 0.31, 'cash-flow' 0.28; 'scale model' 0.02, 'fashion model' 0.00, a climate 'general circulation model' 0.09. 'regression analysis' read 0.21, so the economics framing may matter less than the label says.
